★★★ `cset` AT BOTH WIDTHS, WITH THE UNSIGNED CONDITIONS, RUNNING — the runtime witness `D-ASM-ARM64-SETCC-W-FORM-UNDECLARED` did not have. That row was closed by declaring `setcc` at width 64 (0x9A9F07E0) and width 32 (0x1A9F07E0) and dropping the `width` pin from the twelve `cset` dialect rows, and it is byte-pinned at both widths against `aarch64-linux-gnu-as` 2.42 in `tests/asm/test_asm_shipped_dialects.cpp`. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-15: before this file, NO example under `examples/**` used `cset` in any form, so the entire feature was witnessed by byte pins alone. Byte pins prove the word; only a run proves the word MEANS what the table says.

★★★ WHY THE UNSIGNED CONDITIONS AND NOT `eq`/`ne`. gas spells its unsigned peers `lo`/`ls`/`hi`/`hs` while the substrate spells them `ult`/`ule`/`ugt`/`uge` — the two vocabularies DISAGREE, and `name` beside `cond` in the dialect rows is therefore two facts, not one written twice. A shipped anchor was once FALSELY CLOSED because it was witnessed only on `eq`/`ne`, the two spellings where the vocabularies happen to coincide; a witness built on those cannot see a letter-matching table that maps `ls`->`sle`. Every condition here is chosen where the two DISAGREE.

★★★ THE VALUE IS THE ONE WHERE SIGNED AND UNSIGNED GIVE OPPOSITE ANSWERS. x0 = -1 compared against 1: signed, -1 < 1; unsigned, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF > 1. So `hi` must be 1 and `gt` must be 0 on the SAME comparison — the pair is self-checking, and a table that mapped `hi` onto `sgt` inverts both. ✔MEASURED red-on-disable under qemu-aarch64: changing the single token `cset x1, hi` to `cset x1, gt` moves the exit code from 42 to 10, exactly the 32 that condition carries.

★★ SIX RESULTS ON SIX DISTINCT POWERS OF TWO, so no wrong answer can hide behind another. The three EXPECTED-1 conditions carry 32 (`hi`, X-form), 8 (`hs`, X-form) and 2 (`lo`, W-form) and sum to exactly 42; the three EXPECTED-0 conditions carry 1 (`gt`, X-form), 4 (`lo`, X-form) and 16 (`hi`, W-form) and contribute nothing while they are right. Any single condition answering wrongly moves the exit by its own unique amount, so the exit code NAMES which one broke instead of merely saying 'not 42'.

⚠ WHAT THE RUNTIME ARM CAN AND CANNOT SEE, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN OVERCLAIMED. `CSET Wd,cc` and `CSET Xd,cc` both leave 0 or 1 in the destination with the upper 32 bits clear, so a MIS-ELECTED width would not by itself change this exit code — that election is what the byte pins are for, and this file does not duplicate them. What the W-form lines DO witness is that they lower and execute AT ALL: before the target declared the 32-bit variant, `cset w7, lo` was a LOUD REFUSAL (an absent-width variant matches any width, so the bare row would have elected the one 64-bit variant and emitted the 64-bit word — which is why the `width` pin shipped in the first place). Both widths are therefore on a running path, and the conditions on both are runtime-checked.

★ NO CALL, SO NO LINK-REGISTER DANCE. Unlike `asm_arm64_branch_call`, nothing here calls anything, so x30 is untouched and `main` needs no hand-written preservation. x1..x9 are all caller-saved on AAPCS64, so the entry trampoline's state survives.
★ `mul` BY A WEIGHT REGISTER RATHER THAN `lsl`: ✔MEASURED, `lsl x1, x1, #5` is refused A0008 — the target's `shl` declares no encoding variant accepting a 2-operand immediate shape at width 64. Anchored territory; `mul` is the verified spelling this dialect and target already agree on, and the weighting is arithmetic either way.

★ THE `release` ARM, SCOPED HONESTLY. At the `encode` tier no MIR module exists, so the optimizer, the register allocator and calling-convention materialization never run — this arm does NOT witness the optimizer and cannot. It pins the narrower fact that `--config=release` still produces a working binary, i.e. the release configuration does not BREAK the assembly path.

★★ RED-ON-DISABLE: change any `cset` condition to a neighbouring one -> the exit moves by that condition's own weight (measured: hi->gt gives 10). Delete either `setcc` variant from `arm64.target.json` -> the matching width stops encoding (the W-form reverts to a loud refusal, or the X-form does). Re-add `width` to the twelve `cset` dialect rows -> `effectiveWidth` reconciles the declared 64 against the register-derived 32 and refuses `cset w7, lo`, a line gas takes. Swap a `name` against its `cond` in any dialect row -> that condition inverts and the exit moves.
